title: Inner Join with Join
description: Learn to combine two collections using the Join operator, equivalent to SQL inner join.

data.text: The `Join` operator combines two sequences (collections) based on matching keys and returns a result. It is equivalent to an **inner join** in SQL.
The `Join` extension method has two overloads. The first overload takes five parameters:

data.title: Join Method Signature

items: **outerKeySelector** — Lambda to extract the key from outer sequence
**innerKeySelector** — Lambda to extract the key from inner sequence
**resultSelector** — Lambda to create the result from matching elements

data.title: Join in Method Syntax
Inner Join Behavior
data.text: Only elements with matching keys in both sequences are included in the result. Elements without matches are excluded.
In query syntax, the `Join` operator uses the `on` and `equals` keywords:

data.title: Join in Query Syntax
Use 'equals' not '=='
data.text: In query syntax, use the 'equals' keyword to match keys, not the '==' operator.

data.caption: Inner join returns only matching elements from both collections

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Join combines two sequences based on matching keys
Only elements with matches in both sequences are included
Use 'equals' keyword in query syntax, not '=='
